Don't be fooled by the location and decor, or tour book
Feb 2016 • Family
This is by far the worst restaurant we visited in our 6 day stay in Hanoi. The location is great, right by Opera house, so you would think they are frequent with tourist. Well, not only the waitresses cannot speak any English, even if I just point at the menu to order, the waitress has to go to the bar to ask if they can make it. Most of the drinks or desert we wanted are out of stock. But somehow, all the local Vietnam patrons seems to have the same drinks we wanted. We ended up ordering something they said they have. But only half the order came, while the other half never showed up. When asked for it, the same person ordered for us, thinks that we never ordered them, and tell us it will take very long and suggested us to switch to another item. No idea what is going on. We end up leaving quite frustrated.

Nearly didn't eat!
Apr 2015 • Couples
Good location opposite the opera house. That's about all this place has going for it! As previously mentioned there is pizza on the menu! And some items with beef on them. We ordered. A G&T and a Tom Collins -(Gin based cocktail), 1 Whiskey & 7Up and a Rum cocktail. 2 starters, Crab Rolls & Spring Veg rolls. Mains were spaghetti carbonara. Pork chops BBQ sauce and chips, roast chicken pizza and Beef rolls in mushroom and pepper sauce. Repeated back for confirmation by our server. 10 minutes later it transpired there was no gin ! (2x diet cokes instead then!) 20 minutes after that, there was no cheese for the carbonara!. "but we are getting some and we used the last of the beef"? (Beef rolls changed to chicken and olive pizza ) (it didn't occur to me to ask about the cheese for pizza) our crab rolls arrived - we shared. Spaghetti carbonara arrived, we watched it get eaten. The pork arrived(with cold chips) we watched it get eaten.
Our spring veg rolls arrived - with shrimp and beef in them! We shared. One pizza arrived. 10 minutes later the last pizza arrived with no olives but mushrooms. Call me a Mr picky, but I like to eat starters at the start and mains at the main. And preferably with everyone else. Not a good experience lets just say the tip wasn't monetary. Avoid at all costs unless you are just drinking, and then it can't be gin.

I'd give it a miss
Dec 2014 • Family
The restaurant, located next to a French bistro, looked pretty good, so, regrettably, I opted for it over the French place. I should have known when we entered the restaurant that this wasn't going to be good - it was sparsely populated, for one thing, while the French place was full. Also, I felt sort of duped when the server finally came around with the dusty menus - the outside of the restaurant seemed to suggest that this was an Italian place - I'm sure I saw something about pizza, and about Illy coffee. But no, the pizza they have is decent, not bad but not good, either. And the menu is all over the place - Vietnamese food, western food. The Vietnamese food we ordered was alright. But the restaurant didn't appear to me to be very clean - as I mentioned the menu didn't feel clean - felt like there was grit on it; the decor and general feel of the restaurant seemed dingy. So I had a difficult time enjoying the overall experience. The service was friendly enough. It took them a while, and at times we wondered if they had forgotten about us.

Moderately Priced and Reliable Alternative
Aug 2014 • Couples
If you are staying at the Metropole or exploring the neighborhood of the opera house, here's a place for a moderately priced lunch with a nice atmosphere. The good news is that you are not paying Metropole prices. Stay with the Vietnamese dishes; they have very tasty soups (including snake head fish soup which is near excellent) and traditional noodle dishes. Don't be tempted to leap at a pizza, even if you've been away from the good ol' USA for weeks. It's just not something the Vietnamese understand very well. You can save some serious bucks here and still have a good meal. We had about five lunches and a dinner here, and, except for the pizza, were never disappointed.

Lovely Restaurant In Ha Noi
May 2014 • Couples
I am working in Ha Noi two months and with my wife visiting from abroad I was looking for something special. Sweet Cherry was recommended by a work colleague and is close to work and hotel.

Its a lovely restaurant, with a excellent setting just opposite the opera house. 

They have a wonderfully varied menu of western and Asian dishes including local Vietnamese dishes.

The service was excellent, the food delicious, portions not too big, and the prices reasonable compared to other restaurants we have tried in the same area.

Small reservation was some minor confusion on language understanding, but the serve and food made it well worthwile. My wife is very discerning and has already said she wants to return to Sweet Cherry again before leaving ha Noi.

Well recommended restaurant.
